review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

3:1.sourceText: Ὑπομίμνῃσκε αὐτοὺς ἀρχαῖς ἐξουσίαις ὑποτάσσεσθαι, πειθαρχεῖν, πρὸς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἑτοίμους εἶναι,
3:1.targetText: Remind them to be subject to principalities and authorities, to obey rule, to be ready to every good work,

groups.note: The compound πειθαρχεῖν means obey authority/rule; LSV expands the one actual obedience predicate as to obey rule, without a separate Greek rule noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness connective addition: LSV and between principalities and authorities follows TR καί; pinned N1904 writes the two ruler/authority nouns without a conjunction.

3:2.sourceText: μηδένα βλασφημεῖν, ἀμάχους εἶναι, ἐπιεικεῖς, πᾶσαν ἐνδεικνυμένους πραΰτητα πρὸς πάντας ἀνθρώπους.
3:2.targetText: to speak evil of no one, not to be quarrelsome—gentle, showing all meekness to all men,

groups.note: The negative-compound adjective ἀμάχους means peaceable/not quarrelsome. Its own negative prefix supplies not, distinct from the earlier no-one object.

3:3.sourceText: Ἦμεν γάρ ποτε καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀνόητοι, ἀπειθεῖς, πλανώμενοι, δουλεύοντες ἐπιθυμίαις καὶ ἡδοναῖς ποικίλαις, ἐν κακίᾳ καὶ φθόνῳ διάγοντες, στυγητοί, μισοῦντες ἀλλήλους.
3:3.targetText: for we, also, were once thoughtless, disobedient, led astray, serving manifold desires and pleasures, living in malice and envy, odious—hating one another;

3:4.sourceText: ὅτε δὲ ἡ χρηστότης καὶ ἡ φιλανθρωπία ἐπεφάνη τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Θεοῦ,
3:4.targetText: and when the kindness and the love to men of God our Savior appeared

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

3:5.sourceText: οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων τῶν ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ ἃ ἐποιήσαμεν ἡμεῖς ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὸ αὐτοῦ ἔλεος ἔσωσεν ἡμᾶς διὰ λουτροῦ παλινγενεσίας καὶ ἀνακαινώσεως Πνεύματος Ἁγίου,
3:5.targetText: (not by works that [are] in righteousness that we did but according to His kindness), He saved us, through a bathing of regeneration, and a renewing of the Holy Spirit,

groups.note: LSV kindness here renders the actual mercy noun ἔλεος, distinct from the preceding verse’s actual kindness noun χρηστότης. The different Greek heads are preserved instead of being conflated by the identical English gloss.

3:8.sourceText: Πιστὸς ὁ λόγος, καὶ περὶ τούτων βούλομαί σε διαβεβαιοῦσθαι, ἵνα φροντίζωσιν καλῶν ἔργων προΐστασθαι οἱ πεπιστευκότες Θεῷ. ταῦτά ἐστιν καλὰ καὶ ὠφέλιμα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις·
3:8.targetText: The word [is] steadfast; and concerning these things I intend you to affirm fully, that they may be thoughtful, to be leading in good works—who have believed God; these are the good and profitable things to men,

groups.note: The leading/taking-care-of infinitive προΐστασθαι governs good works as a genitive complement; LSV expresses this as to be leading in good works. The English in marks that complement relation without a separately written Greek in preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.
English adds the definite article to the recast good-and-profitable-things predicate; N1904 has predicative quality adjectives without an article there.

English supplies the nominal head things for its good-and-profitable-things predicate. The Greek line says these are good and profitable, with no second independent thing noun; the actual initial demonstrative remains these.

review.note: The exact good and profitable heads remain separate. English recasts Greek predicative adjectives as modifiers of a supplied things noun; that grammatical support is explained without merging their distinct lexical identities.

3:9.sourceText: μωρὰς δὲ ζητήσεις καὶ γενεαλογίας καὶ ἔριν καὶ μάχας νομικὰς περιΐστασο· εἰσὶν γὰρ ἀνωφελεῖς καὶ μάταιοι.
3:9.targetText: but stand away from foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about law—for they are unprofitable and vain.

groups.note: Pinned N1904 ἔριν is singular contention/strife, while LSV uses plural contentions as the TR plural ἔρεις. The lexical dispute head is retained with this number difference explicit.

3:10.sourceText: αἱρετικὸν ἄνθρωπον μετὰ μίαν καὶ δευτέραν νουθεσίαν παραιτοῦ,
3:10.targetText: Reject a heretical man, after a first and second admonition,

groups.note: The actual adjective αἱρετικόν describes a factious/divisive person; LSV uses heretical. The link retains the underlying divisiveness head without assuming that the source word necessarily carries every later technical doctrinal sense of heresy.
Greek μίαν is one, used with second to designate the first admonition; LSV renders its ordinal role as first.

3:11.sourceText: εἰδὼς ὅτι ἐξέστραπται ὁ τοιοῦτος καὶ ἁμαρτάνει, ὢν αὐτοκατάκριτος.
3:11.targetText: having known that he has been subverted who [is] such, and sins, being self-condemned.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplies the who-is-such designation; Greek has article plus such without a separate being verb at that nominal phrase. The later actual ὢν supplies being with self-condemned.

3:12.sourceText: Ὅταν πέμψω Ἀρτεμᾶν πρὸς σὲ ἢ Τυχικόν, σπούδασον ἐλθεῖν πρός με εἰς Νικόπολιν· ἐκεῖ γὰρ κέκρικα παραχειμάσαι.
3:12.targetText: When I will send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, be diligent to come to me to Nicopolis, for I have determined to winter there.

groups.note: The Greek sending verb πέμψω is aorist subjunctive after when, while LSV expresses the anticipated event as I will send. The same actual sending action remains linked without changing its original mood.

3:13.sourceText: Ζηνᾶν τὸν νομικὸν καὶ Ἀπολλῶν σπουδαίως πρόπεμψον, ἵνα μηδὲν αὐτοῖς λείπῃ.
3:13.targetText: Diligently send forth Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way, that nothing to them may be lacking,

groups.note: The sending-onward verb πρόπεμψον includes forwarding/equipping people on a journey; LSV expands the full predicate as send forth ... on their way. Their identifies the two named travelers in that English predicate, not a separate printed original possessive pronoun. The two actual names keep their distinct lexical anchors.

3:14.sourceText: μανθανέτωσαν δὲ καὶ οἱ ἡμέτεροι καλῶν ἔργων προΐστασθαι εἰς τὰς ἀναγκαίας χρείας, ἵνα μὴ ὦσιν ἄκαρποι.
3:14.targetText: and let them learn—ours also—to be leading in good works to the necessary uses, that they may not be unfruitful.

groups.note: The substantive article/possessive phrase οἱ ἡμέτεροι means our people/those belonging to us; English renders the complete designation ours.

The leading/maintaining infinitive governs the genitive good-works complement; LSV expresses that governed relation as to be leading in, without a separate original in preposition. The actual good and works heads remain separately linked.
